tao2024llms: LLMs often answer questions wrong or admit uncertainty even though their parameters hold the correct answer. Internal-representation analysis shows correct answers frequently appear among high-probability tokens but are not selected. Hits@k measures such latent knowledge retention independently of surface accuracy, revealing that models store far more knowledge than their QA scores suggest. SkipUnsure then recovers detected-but-unexpressed knowledge without retraining, improving accuracy by up to 11.8 percent on DBPedia and 6.3 percent on IMDB across open-domain and domain-specific QA datasets.
tao2025how: Few-shot LLMs often generate invalid SMILES strings for molecules, and SELFIES, in which every string is a valid molecule, surprisingly works worse than SMILES for LLMs, while direct self-correction of invalid strings is weak. SmiSelf converts an invalid SMILES into SELFIES using grammatical rules and exploits SELFIES' guarantee to repair it, then maps back. The framework ensures 100 percent validity while preserving molecular properties and maintaining or improving other generation metrics, and it is compatible with any SMILES-based generative model, broadening practical LLM use in drug discovery.
tao2025understanding: GUI agents ground language into screen coordinates, but multimodal models hallucinate locations systematically. A fine-grained evaluation splits predictions into four error types, exposing failures hidden by plain accuracy. The Peak Sharpness Score measures how well semantic continuity aligns with the coordinate logit distribution, quantifying uncertainty in localization. Context-Aware Cropping, a training-free technique, adaptively crops the input around likely regions and improves grounding. Together the evaluation and method reveal when and why GUI agents drift and make their behavior more interpretable and robust.
tao2026arellmsknowledgeable: LLMs underperform on QA not only because of missing knowledge but because they keep correct answers buried in the distribution. Token-level analysis finds correct answers often among high-probability candidates yet unselected, and Hits@k measures this latent retention independent of surface form. The work further shows that few-shot prompts allowing unsure outputs suppress low-confidence correct answers, and quantitative experiments isolate this suppression effect. The findings explain why models appear less knowledgeable than they are and give guidance for prompting and decoding in knowledge-intensive tasks.
tao2026mitigating: High-resolution inputs break visual positional encodings in multimodal models, and the failure is not random: it pushes coordinate predictions toward predictable internal spatial priors. VPSG is a training-free inference-time fix that shuffles visual positional embeddings to expose the position-unconditioned bias, then uses this negative evidence to steer digit decoding through a lightweight finite-state machine. On ScreenSpot-Pro it reduces coordinate drift and improves localization across model scales without retraining.
tao2026rectifying: Precise coordinate grounding is hard for multimodal models because high-resolution inputs degrade visual positional encodings, producing directional rather than random errors as the model falls back on internal spatial priors. Counterfactual positional guidance shuffles the visual positional embeddings at inference to isolate the position-unconditioned tendency and subtracts it while decoding digits through a small finite-state controller. This training-free correction narrows coordinate drift on ScreenSpot-Pro and improves localization accuracy at multiple model scales, showing that positional-encoding failures are diagnosable and reversible.
tao2026viewfusion: Multi-view reasoning is fragile because models ignore cross-view relations and rely on single-image shortcuts. ViewFusion separates spatial alignment from answering: a first stage reasons explicitly about viewpoint relations and transformations across views into an intermediate workspace, then a second stage answers questions conditioned on that workspace. Trained with synthetic spatial supervision and GRPO reinforcement learning, it stabilizes the two-stage behavior. On MMSI-Bench it beats Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct by 5.3 percent, with the largest gains on examples requiring genuine cross-view alignment and handling of occlusion.
tong2026autagent: Audio LLMs perceive well but fail at precise acoustic measurements, and using every available tool overloads the context while prompt-based tool selection cannot judge context-dependent utility. AuTAgent is a reinforcement-learning agent that learns when and which acoustic tools to call, trained with sparse feedback and a Differential Reward that rewards tool use only when it beats the base model. On MMAU Test-mini and MMAR it improves accuracy by 4.2 and 6.2 percent for open-source and 9.8 and 8.0 percent for closed-source backbones, and transfers well to new tasks, showing tools complement audio model reasoning.
wang2017using: DBpedia encodes logical relations between named entities, while Twitter records how often entities are mentioned together. The work asks whether semantic paths in the knowledge graph can explain co-occurrence frequencies on Twitter. A ranking function is trained over paths containing a single intermediate entity, using lexical, graph-embedding, and popularity features, to score which path best explains why two entities appear in the same tweet. The results show knowledge-graph relations complement social-media mention statistics, letting semantic structure explain observed entity co-occurrence.
wang2020detecting: GCN node classifiers suffer silent implementation bugs that compile and run normally yet degrade accuracy, because the contribution of node features and graph structure is opaque. A metamorphic-testing approach compares input-output pairs rather than checking single cases, with formal justification, to expose such bugs. An adaptive pipeline overlaps CPU and GPU work. It detects over 80 percent of synthetic mutants and two real bugs in GCN implementations while running more than ten times faster than a sequential pipeline, offering a practical way to test graph learning systems.
wang2020graphcrop: Omitting a substructure usually does not change a graph's label, so subgraph cropping simulates that real-world noise as data augmentation. GraphCrop keeps a connected, node-centric cropped subgraph with valid context, encouraging GNNs to read global structure rather than memorize a few key nodes or edges. Parameter-free and easy to add to existing classifiers, it creates informative labeled graphs and yields consistent gains on standard graph-classification benchmarks.
wang2020nodeaug: Data augmentation for graphs is hard because edges couple nodes, so augmenting one node changes others and can shift labels. NodeAug builds a parallel universe for each node so augmentations do not interfere, and regularizes every node's prediction to be invariant to its own augmented features and structure. Three augmentation strategies alter attributes and edges, and subgraph mini-batch training feeds only each batch's receptive fields rather than the whole graph. On Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, and two co-authorship networks it improves strong GCNs while training more efficiently.
